findings.technique: Key-shape method dispatch: pick a specialized hash table per GROUP BY key layout (the 'method zoo')
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Interpreters/AggregatedDataVariants.cpp:230-439 (chooseAggregationMethod), AggregatedDataVariants.h:62-138 (variant fields), AggregatedData.h:34-70 (table typedefs)
findings.mechanism: Exact decision tree: keys_size==0 -> without_key. Single non-nullable numeric key by byte width: 1->key8 (FixedImplicitZeroHashMapWithCalculatedSize<UInt8,AggregateDataPtr>, a 256-slot direct-address array, no hashing), 2->key16 (FixedHashMap, 65536 slots), 4->key32 / 8->key64 (open-addressing HashMap with HashCRC32 hardware-CRC hash), 16->keys128, 32->keys256 (HashMap<UInt128/UInt256, UInt128HashCRC32>). Multiple fixed-width keys: pack all key bytes contiguously (packFixed in AggregationCommon.h:94-246, incl. SSSE3 packFixedShuffle) and route on total bytes: <=2->keys16 (direct-address FixedHashMap over the packed UInt16!), <=4->keys32, <=8->keys64, <=16->keys128, <=32->keys256. Nullable keys fold a null bitmap into the packed blob: KeysNullMap<UInt128>+key_bytes<=16 -> nullable_keys128, <=32 -> nullable_keys256. Single String -> key_packed_string (HashMap<PackedStringRef>) or key_string (5-way StringHashMap); FixedString -> key_fixed_string. Anything else: if all keys are numbers/strings -> prealloc_serialized, else serialized (key = arena-serialized byte blob, HashMapWithSavedHash<string_view>). Separate *_hash64 variants (full 64-bit hash) exist only for external/spill merging where >4B keys are possible. Growers: HashTableGrowerWithPrecalculation (HashTable.h:272-318) starts at 2^8 cells, max load factor 0.5 (maxFill = bufSize/2), grows by 4x below 2^23 cells then 2x.
findings.maps_to: B3 (string/multi-col group keys; per-group boxed accumulators)
findings.our_implementation: Replace the thread-local HashMap<u64, Vec<AccumulatorState>> fallback in src/physical/morsel_agg.rs / hash_agg.rs with a Rust enum-dispatched GroupTable chosen at plan time from Arrow key types: PackedU16 (direct-address Vec of dense group ids, 65536 slots), PackedU32/PackedU64 (open-addressing u64 table with crc32/xxh3), PackedU128 for <=16 total key bytes (covers Q10's post-GroupKeyReduction keys, Q16 brand+type+size after dict-encoding size), and SerializedBytes only as last resort. We already have raw_key() u64 extraction; the missing pieces are the <=2-byte direct-address tier and the 128-bit packed tier so multi-column keys never hit the ScalarValue/Vec path.
findings.est_payoff: High for the HashMap-path queries: Q10 (894ms, 9.8x native), Q13 (563ms), Q16 (286ms), Q22 (431ms) all group on multi/string keys today. ClickHouse's packed tiers turn per-row key building into 1-2 integer stores + one probe; expect 1.5-2.5x on the aggregation phase of these queries (Q10's agg is the dominant non-scan cost).
findings.effort: Medium: ~1-2 weeks. Key packing from Arrow arrays is straightforward; the dispatch enum touches planner + both agg operators.

findings.technique: FixedHashTable direct-address aggregation with inline COUNT state and per-function batch loops (addBatchLookupTable8)
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:1096-1147 (key8 special case), 226-234 (getInlineCountState), .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/HashTable/FixedHashTable.h:113-134, 388-417 (NUM_CELLS=1<<size_bits, min/max populated-range tracking)
findings.mechanism: For an 8-bit key, method.data.data() is literally a 256-entry array of 8-byte mapped slots. Pure COUNT(*) becomes `UInt64* map = data(); for(i) ++map[key[i]];` — the AggregateDataPtr slot itself IS the counter (getInlineCountState reinterprets the pointer cell as UInt64), so there is zero arena allocation and zero indirection. For real aggregate functions, addBatchLookupTable8 (IAggregateFunction.h) runs ONE aggregate function over the whole batch against the 256-slot LUT before moving to the next function (column-at-a-time over functions, not row-at-a-time). FixedHashTable tracks min/max occupied index (FixedHashTable.h:122-123) so result iteration scans only [min,max] instead of all 2^16 cells for key16.
findings.maps_to: B3 (we have a perfect-hash array for <=256 groups already, but not the inline-count or 65536-slot tier)
findings.our_implementation: Extend our perfect-hash tier from <=256 groups to any packed key <=16 bits (65536 slots of flat accumulator state = a few MB, L2-resident), with min/max occupied tracking for cheap finalize. Store COUNT directly in the slot (we already do flat counts in VectorizedGroupTable — carry that into the morsel path for all group-count shapes). Run one accumulator column over the whole 8K batch before the next (we partially do this; make it universal).
findings.est_payoff: Moderate: mostly benefits 2-key small-domain aggregations (Q01 flag+status packs into 2 bytes = direct-address without our current dictionary-dependent perfect-hash heuristic; Q12 shipmode+linestatus similar). Removes branchy group-id resolution; expect tens of ms on Q01/Q12-class aggregations, and it simplifies the fast path.
findings.effort: Low: days. It composes with finding 1's PackedU16 tier.

findings.technique: Two-level (256-bucket) hash table with lazy conversion and bucket-parallel work-stealing merge
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/HashTable/TwoLevelHashTable.h:18-100 (NUM_BUCKETS=1<<8, getBucketFromHash = (hash>>(32-8))&255), .scratch/clickhouse/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:83-127 (worthConvertToTwoLevel + initDataVariantsWithSizeHint), 1724-1731 (post-block conversion), 2924-2980 (prepareChunksAndFillTwoLevelImpl), 3432+ (mergeBucketImpl)
findings.mechanism: Each thread aggregates into a SINGLE-level table first. After every block, if result_size >= group_by_two_level_threshold (default 100000 keys; 0 when single-threaded so conversion never happens) or memory >= group_by_two_level_threshold_bytes, the table is converted in place to 256 sub-tables keyed by the top byte of the low 32 hash bits (defaults are from Core/Settings, not in this sparse checkout). All threads use the SAME hash function, so bucket b of every thread contains the same key partition; final merge is: atomic counter next_bucket_to_merge.fetch_add(1), each pool thread claims a bucket, merges that bucket across all thread-local tables (mergeBucketImpl) and immediately converts it to an output chunk (convertOneBucketToChunk) using its own Arena — no locks, no repartition pass, results stream out bucket by bucket. mergeDataImpl (Aggregator.cpp:3089-3182) merges via mergeToViaEmplace: on key collision it collects dst_place/src_place pairs into two PaddedPODArrays, then calls each function's mergeAndDestroyBatch once over the whole pair array (batched, not per-key virtual calls). A cross-query statistics cache (initDataVariantsWithSizeHint/getSizeHint) remembers the observed cardinality and pre-initializes two-level + reserve to median size, skipping the growth/rehash sequence entirely on repeat queries.
findings.maps_to: B3 (our range-partitioned merge does a repartition of finished maps; growth/rehash cost on 15M-group Q18-class tables)
findings.our_implementation: Adopt hash-high-byte bucketing: when a thread-local table crosses ~100K groups, split it into 256 sub-maps by hash byte (cheap: rehash once, or store hash per entry and drain). Merge phase = rayon work-stealing over bucket indices, each task merging bucket b from all thread locals and emitting a finished RecordBatch immediately (streams into parent operator, reducing peak memory). Add a per-(query-shape, table) cardinality memo so repeated benchmark runs pre-size tables.
findings.est_payoff: Moderate-to-high on high-cardinality aggs: Q13 (1.5M custkey groups x N threads) and the HashMap paths of Q10/Q15 currently pay a serial-ish merge + rehash; bucket-parallel merge typically saves 20-40% of merge time and removes the final concat. Q18 already uses the dense-array path so unaffected.
findings.effort: Medium: ~1 week inside morsel_agg.rs merge machinery.

findings.technique: Aggregate state = one contiguous arena 'row' per group, place-pointer mapped values, two-pass batch execution (resolve places, then addBatch per function)
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.h:394-401 (offsets_of_aggregate_states, total_size_of_aggregate_states, align_aggregate_states), Aggregator.cpp:828-858 (createAggregateStates), 1208-1319 (places[] resolution loop), 1321-1380 (executeAggregateInstructions), .scratch/clickhouse/src/AggregateFunctions/IAggregateFunction.h:167-190,325-375 (create/sizeOfData/alignOfData/addBatch/addBatchSinglePlace), .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/Arena.h:152 (4KB initial chunk, 2x growth, 128MB linear threshold)
findings.mechanism: At Aggregator construction, offsets of every aggregate function's POD state are laid out into one struct-like row (total_size_of_aggregate_states, aligned to max alignment). Hash table maps key -> AggregateDataPtr (raw char*) bump-allocated from an Arena; createAggregateStates placement-constructs each state at place+offset. The hot loop is strictly two passes per batch: pass 1 walks rows doing emplaceKey and fills an AggregateDataPtr places[row] array (allocating+initializing state rows only on first insert); pass 2 calls, for EACH aggregate function separately, inst->batch_that->addBatch(row_begin,row_end,places,state_offset,args,...) — one virtual call per function per 8K batch, with the inner loop reading one argument column sequentially and scattering into places[i]+offset. Merging likewise batches: collect place pairs, one mergeAndDestroyBatch call per function.
findings.maps_to: B3 (our 'per-group heap-boxed accumulator vectors' in the HashMap paths)
findings.our_implementation: Kill Vec<AccumulatorState> per group. Two viable Rust ports: (a) exact CH port — bump-arena (bumpalo or chunked Vec<u8>) rows with precomputed field offsets, table maps packed key -> u32 offset into arena; (b) more idiomatic: table maps key -> dense u32 group_id, accumulators live in parallel flat Vec<f64>/Vec<i64> columns (struct-of-arrays; we already do this in VectorizedGroupTable) — SoA is strictly better for our column-at-a-time updates and avoids alignment bookkeeping. Either way, keep the two-pass structure: resolve group_ids[0..8192] first, then run each accumulator column over the batch (sequential column read, scatter by group_id).
findings.est_payoff: High wherever the HashMap fallback runs: removes one heap allocation + pointer chase per group and per-row enum dispatch on accumulator type. On Q10/Q13/Q16/Q22 aggregation phases expect 1.5-2x; also shrinks merge cost since state rows memcpy/merge in batch.
findings.effort: Medium: the SoA variant is an extension of existing VectorizedGroupTable to all key shapes — pairs naturally with finding 1.

findings.technique: StringHashTable: 5-way length-class dispatch with strings-as-integers keys and saved-hash only for long strings
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/HashTable/StringHashTable.h:10-18 (StringKey8=UInt64, StringKey16=UInt128, StringKey24=3xUInt64), 240-298 (m0/m1/m2/m3/ms sub-tables), 325-417 (dispatch), .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/HashTable/StringHashMap.h:20-73 (cells; std::string_view cell = HashMapCellWithSavedHash)
findings.mechanism: One logical string map is five physical tables: m0 = dedicated empty-string slot; m1 = keys 1-8 bytes packed into a UInt64; m2 = 9-16 bytes into UInt128; m3 = 17-24 bytes into {UInt64 a,b,c}; ms = >=25 bytes (or strings with a trailing NUL, which are unrepresentable after zero-padding) as string_view cells that SAVE the 64-bit hash (compare saved hash before memcmp; no rehash on resize). Dispatch (StringHashTable.h:335-417) is branch-lean: switch((sz-1)>>3); always memcpy 8 bytes at a time; tail bytes zeroed by shift s=(-sz&7)*8; for 1-8B keys it checks (ptr & 2048)==0 to decide whether reading 8 bytes forward is safe within the half-page, else reads the LAST 8 bytes and shifts — avoiding any per-byte copy loop. Short keys store NO hash and NO pointer: the packed integer is the cell key, equality is 1-3 integer compares, and 'zero cell' is encoded as last-word==0 (impossible for a real key). Hash for each class is CRC32-based over the fixed words (StringHashTableHash:46-67). Sub-tables grow independently (reserve splits /4).
findings.maps_to: B3 (string group keys: Q10 c_phone/c_address are pass-through, Q16 p_brand/p_type, Q22 cntrycode), and B2 (string join keys, e.g. p_name-less joins with string keys)
findings.our_implementation: In Rust over Arrow StringArray: classify each key by (len-1)>>3 into u64 / u128 / [u64;3] inline keys (memcpy from the values buffer + shift-mask — offsets give us len for free; Arrow buffers are padded so the 8-byte overread is safe without CH's page trick, or use the last-8-bytes read for safety). Four flat open-addressing tables + empty-slot. Practically ALL TPC-H strings fit <=24 bytes (brands 8, modes 7, nations <=15, phone 15, cntrycode 2), so the saved-hash long path is cold. This drops per-key allocation, hashing over bytes, and memcmp from the group/join key path.
findings.est_payoff: High for Q16 (286ms, 7.3x) and Q22 (431ms, 12.6x) whose group keys are strings; also trims Q10's serialized-key cost. Integer-compare probes typically 2-3x faster than string_view probes at TPC-H string lengths.
findings.effort: Medium: self-contained data structure, ~1 week including the agg + join integrations.

findings.technique: LowCardinality execution: aggregate on dictionary INDICES with a per-dictionary place cache and cached per-dictionary hashes
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/ColumnsHashing.h:33-103 (LowCardinalityDictionaryCache: saved_hash per dictionary keyed by {dict hash, size}), 82-330 (HashMethodSingleLowCardinalityColumn: mapped_cache, visit_cache, getIndexAt, emplaceKey/findKey), .scratch/clickhouse/src/Columns/ColumnLowCardinality.h:19-67 (dictionary + UIntXX index column layout), AggregatedDataVariants.h:123-138 (low_cardinality_* method variants)
findings.mechanism: The key column stays as (dictionary, index[UInt8/16/32/64]) — never materialized. Per block: mapped_cache (AggregateDataPtr per dictionary position) and visit_cache (Empty/Found/NotFound per position) are sized to the dictionary. emplaceKey(row): idx=index[row]; if visit_cache[idx]==Found -> return mapped_cache[idx] with ZERO hash-table work. Only the FIRST occurrence of each distinct dictionary position per block touches the real hash table, and even then it passes saved_hash[idx] — a per-dictionary hash array computed once and cached ACROSS blocks in LowCardinalityDictionaryCache keyed by (dictionary UInt128 hash, size), so shared/repeated dictionaries never rehash. Null is dictionary position 0 (special-cased). Net cost per row on a 60M-row/3K-dict column: one index load + one cache-array load.
findings.maps_to: B1 + B3 (this is exactly our PARITY-PLAN 'dictionary-aware strings' rewrite) and B2 (dictionary join keys)
findings.our_implementation: Read parquet string columns as Arrow DictionaryArray (arrow-rs supports this natively; parquet dictionary pages pass through without decode-to-flat — also cuts B1 decode bytes). In morsel_agg: when a group key is dictionary-encoded, group on the u32 keys() indices; keep a per-(dictionary ptr) Vec<group_id> place cache so the hash table is touched once per distinct dict value per batch; hash the dictionary values once per file/row-group (dictionaries are per-column-chunk stable) and reuse. Finalize resolves indices back to strings once, for the few thousand output groups.
findings.est_payoff: Highest single lever for string queries: Q01's returnflag/linestatus, Q10 nation, Q12 shipmode, Q16 brand/type all become integer aggregations, and skipping flat-string materialization directly attacks B1's 250ms Q01 decode. DuckDB's parity on these queries rests on the same trick. Expect 2x+ on string-key agg phases and 30-50% decode reduction on dict-heavy scans.
findings.effort: High: touches scan (dict passthrough), expression eval on dict arrays, and agg — but it is already the planned Phase-1 parity rewrite; CH's mapped_cache/visit_cache/saved-hash triple is the concrete design to copy.

findings.technique: JIT-fused aggregate update loop: one compiled loop applies ALL aggregate functions' adds per row (we'd monomorphize instead of JIT)
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Interpreters/JIT/compileFunction.cpp:235-560 (compileCreateAggregateStatesFunctions, compileAddIntoAggregateStatesFunctions Multiple/SinglePlace, compileMergeAggregatesStates, compileInsertAggregatesIntoResultColumns), Aggregator.cpp:750-823 (trigger: compile_aggregate_expressions, min_count_to_compile_aggregate_expression seen-count gate, SipHash-keyed cache), 1268-1283 (JIT create on insert), 1332-1362 (executeAggregateInstructions choosing single-place vs multi-place compiled fn)
findings.mechanism: For each compilable function set (Sum/Avg/Count/Min/Max etc. expose compileAdd emitting LLVM IR, e.g. AggregateFunctionAvg.h:406-433 adds to numerator/denominator), CH emits ONE function: loop over rows { place = places[i]; for each fn: load its argument column element, update state at place+fn_offset }. This inverts the interpreted structure (per-function batch passes) into a single fused pass — one load of places[i], all states on the same cache line updated together, no virtual calls. A single-place variant (all rows -> one state) is selected when all keys are const OR the batch had only one distinct key since cache reset (can_optimize_equal_keys_ranges + hasOnlyOneValueSinceLastReset, Aggregator.cpp:1351-1356). Create/merge/insert-into-result loops are also compiled. Compilation is gated: only after the same function-set hash is seen min_count_to_compile_aggregate_expression times (default 3), then cached process-wide.
findings.maps_to: B3 (Q01: 7 accumulator updates per row currently dispatch per accumulator kind)
findings.our_implementation: No LLVM needed: monomorphize. Define trait FusedAccumulators { fn update_row(&mut self, group: u32, cols: &Cols, row: usize) } and generate (macro or const-generic tuples) fused kernels for the hot combos — Q01 is (Sum f64 x3, SumProd x2 fused as computed cols, Avg x3 sharing one count, Count): a single struct of SoA arrays updated in one row pass. Planner picks a fused kernel when all accumulators are primitive sum/count/min/max/avg over f64/i64 (covers 21/22 TPC-H queries); fall back to the generic path otherwise. Also port the 'single distinct key since reset' short-circuit to addBatchSinglePlace-style column-sum kernels (SIMD sum of a whole batch into one state) — big for near-sorted keys.
findings.est_payoff: Q01's aggregate loop is our second-largest B3 cost after decode; CH measured ~1.2-2x on multi-aggregate loops from this fusion (removes N-1 passes over places[] and all dyn dispatch). Against Q01's ~180ms non-decode time, expect 40-80ms back; also helps Q18's per-group updates.
findings.effort: Medium: macro-generated kernels for ~6 accumulator combos; no new infra.

findings.technique: Adaptive hash-table prefetch with measured look-ahead, gated on table size > L2

The look-ahead distance is not a constant: PrefetchingHelper times the first ~iterationsToMeasure() iterations and derives look-ahead from observed per-row cost. Prefetch is enabled ONLY when (a) the hash table buffer exceeds L2 (below that it is cache-resident and prefetch is pure overhead — comment at Aggregator.cpp:221-223), and (b) the key is cheap to recompute (has_cheap_key_holder; serialized keys would allocate twice, comment at 1011). Same pattern is applied in bucket merges (mergeBucketImpl at 3432-3442: prefetch when NUM_BUCKETS * bucket_buffer > threshold).
findings.maps_to: B2 (join probe: random access into build-side table) and B3 (Q18-class 15M-group tables, our stated hash-probe latency floor)
findings.our_implementation: In VectorizedHashTable::probe_vectorized and the morsel agg group-resolve loop: we already compute batch hashes up front, so issue core::arch::x86_64::_mm_prefetch of slot (hash & mask) 16-64 slots ahead while probing slot i (two-stage: prefetch slot array, then prefetch entry payload). Gate on table_bytes > 1.25MB (L2) exactly like CH. Skip the adaptive timer initially — a fixed look-ahead of ~32 captures most of the win.
findings.est_payoff: Directly attacks our stated 'hash-probe latency floor': DRAM-bound probe loops typically gain 1.3-1.8x from prefetch at 15M+ entries. Targets Q18 agg (187ms), Q09 probe (1.5s), Q13. Cheapest lever in this list per line of code.
findings.effort: Low: days; no data-structure changes.

findings.technique: Consecutive-identical-key cache (LastElementCache) with hit-rate feedback
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Common/ColumnsHashingImpl.h:49-100 (LastElementCacheStats, LastElementCache), 189-450 (HashMethodBase emplace/find consulting cache), Aggregator.cpp mergeOnBlockSmall/consecutive_keys_cache_stats plumbing (Aggregator.cpp:926), 1316 (state.hasOnlyOneValueSinceLastReset feeding the JIT single-place path)

findings.our_implementation: In the group-id resolution loop: keep last_raw_key + last_group_id; compare-first. Add a batch pre-scan (cheap SIMD equality of key column against first element) that routes single-key batches to a fused whole-batch reduction. Parquet row groups sorted by the group key (orders/lineitem by key at generation) make this hit constantly.
findings.est_payoff: Small-to-moderate generally, but near-free; on clustered keys (Q18's l_orderkey groups average 4 consecutive rows) it eliminates ~75% of probes. Complements the dense-range path where domains exceed 64M.
findings.effort: Low: 1-2 days.

findings.technique: Statistics-fed initial sizing of aggregation hash tables (skip growth/rehash entirely on repeated shapes)
findings.source: .scratch/clickhouse/src/Interpreters/Aggregator.cpp:107-127 (initDataVariantsWithSizeHint: getSizeHint(stats_collecting_params, tables_cnt=max_threads) -> init two-level up front + reserve median_size), 130+ (updateStatistics after execution), TwoLevelHashTable.h:99-103 (size_hint constructor reserving size/256 per bucket)

Next execution of the same shape: if the recorded cardinality already exceeds the two-level threshold, the table is CREATED two-level (no mid-flight conversion), and every sub-table reserves median_size/256 cells — so the entire run does zero rehashes. worthConvertToTwoLevel is also consulted with the hint's sum_of_sizes.
findings.maps_to: B3 (rehash/growth of 1.5M+ group tables on Q13/Q10; also our benchmark loop re-runs identical queries)
findings.our_implementation: Keep a small process-level map {(table, group-key column ids, filter fingerprint) -> observed NDV per thread} updated after each agg; on planning, pre-reserve thread-local tables (we already have footer-stats NDV for single columns — this adds the observed-actual feedback loop that fixes composite-key NDV, where our current 'max of per-column NDVs' heuristic under/over-shoots).
findings.est_payoff: Moderate: growth from 256 cells to 2^21 does ~11 rehash passes over live data; pre-sizing saves 10-20% of build time on Q13-class aggs and stabilizes latencies. Trivially helps our repeated-iteration benchmarks.
findings.effort: Low: days; plumbing an execution-feedback map into the planner.

findings.technique: Multi-step PREWHERE: split AND-conjuncts into per-column-set filter steps, cost-ordered, each step reads only its own columns

findings.maps_to: B1 (parquet decode volume)

Staged: shipdate alone (60M) -> ~15% survive -> discount+quantity decode ~9M rows. Cuts predicate-column decode ~60%, est. 30-50ms off Q06; similar shape on Q12/Q14/Q19 (each 150-350ms). Suite-level est. 0.3-0.6s.
findings.effort: low (1-2 days): conjunct splitting already exists in predicate_pushdown.rs; ordering needs only footer column byte sizes + existing selectivity estimates

findings.maps_to: B5 (and B1 decode throughput)

findings.effort: medium-high (each codec is small — Delta is ~30 lines each way — but writer+reader+stats plumbing across the sidecar is the cost)

findings.technique: SelectedPositions (selection vectors) through filter->project with adaptive conjunct reordering
findings.source: .scratch/trino/core/trino-main/src/main/java/io/trino/operator/project/SelectedPositions.java, PageProcessor.java (createWorkProcessor, projectBatchSize adaptation MIN/MAX_PAGE_SIZE 4MB/16MB, MAX_BATCH_SIZE 8192), sql/gen/columnar/AndFilterEvaluator.java + FilterReorderingProfiler.java

findings.technique: Dynamic filters: exact distinct-set domains with graceful min/max degradation + probe-side selectivity-profiled drop

findings.technique: Parquet null decode: chunk-level no-null fast path, word-based validity, temp-buffer scatter
findings.source: .scratch/trino/lib/trino-parquet/src/main/java/io/trino/parquet/reader/flat/FlatColumnReader.java (isNonNull, readNonNull vs readNullable, DataValuesBuffer.readNullableValues), flat/NullsDecoders.java, reader/PageReader.java (hasNoNulls = columnStatistics.getNumNulls()==0)
findings.mechanism: Reader picks one of two entirely separate code paths per column chunk: if field is required OR chunk stats say numNulls==0, definition levels are never decoded at all (readNonNull: values stream straight into the output buffer). Nullable path: def levels decode directly into long[] validity words (RLE runs become word-wide setBits, bit-packed groups OR'd in — never per-bit branches); `validityMaterialized` flag defers touching the validity array until the first null actually appears; chunks that are partially null decode dense values into a temporary buffer sized nonNullCount then a single unpackNullValues scatter positions them; all-null batch -> RLE null block, no buffer at all. findings.maps_to: B1 (decode path). TPC-H columns are all non-null, so the key check is the numNulls==0 chunk fast path.
findings.our_implementation: Mostly already inside arrow-rs (it has skip_def_levels for required fields). Verify with a profile that arrow-rs 53 takes the null-free path for our generator's parquet (columns must be written as REQUIRED or with statistics; if our writer marks them OPTIONAL without stats, arrow-rs decodes def levels for 60M rows for nothing — check tpch/generator.rs writer properties and set required fields / enable statistics). This is a config/writer fix, not an engine rewrite; also relevant to the planned IPC sidecar generator.
findings.est_payoff: Low-medium but nearly free: if def-level decode is currently running on required-but-optional-schema columns, saving is ~1 byte-scan per value per column (~10-30ms/query at SF10).
findings.effort: Low (half day: inspect writer schema nullability + arrow-rs path taken).

findings.technique: Batched group-id assignment API with hoisted capacity checks and reusable buffers

findings.effort: Low (1-2 days), independent of the full flat-record table.

findings.technique: Whole-batch join-position precomputation with branchless null compaction and RLE probe collapse
findings.source: .scratch/trino/core/trino-main/src/main/java/io/trino/operator/join/nonspilling/JoinProbe.java (fillCache, getIsNull: 'nonNullCount += isNull[i] ? 0 : 1', hasOnlyRleBlocks), join/JoinHash.java (getJoinPosition(int[] positions, ..., long[] result))

Output iteration then walks the cache without touching the hash table again (important when join filters cause re-iteration via position links).
findings.maps_to: B2 (our probe interleaves lookup with output row emission)
findings.our_implementation: We mostly do batch probing already; adopt (a) the constant-key batch detection: if the probe key array's min==max in batch stats or is a single-value DictionaryArray/RLE, do one lookup and broadcast; (b) branchless null-compaction before probing instead of per-row null branch inside the probe loop; (c) keep the positions cache so Semi/Anti and filtered joins re-iterate without re-probing.
findings.est_payoff: Low-medium: a few percent on join queries; the RLE collapse is notable after highly-selective dim filters (Q17 brand, Q19).
findings.effort: Low (about 1 day).

findings.technique: Adaptive parquet read batch sizing (ramp-up + byte-bounded)
findings.source: .scratch/trino/lib/trino-parquet/src/main/java/io/trino/parquet/reader/ParquetReader.java (INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE=1, BATCH_SIZE_GROWTH_FACTOR=2, nextBatch(), line 729-734 maxCombinedBytesPerRow clamp), ParquetReaderOptions (DEFAULT_MAX_READ_BLOCK_SIZE=16MB, DEFAULT_MAX_READ_BLOCK_ROW_COUNT=8192)

findings.effort: Low (half day).

findings.technique: Filter pushdown INTO decode kernels: specialized (encoding x validity x mask) kernels + measured pre/post-filter cost heuristic
findings.source: .scratch/polars/crates/polars-parquet/src/arrow/read/deserialize/primitive/plain/mod.rs (decode_aligned_bytes_dispatch matching (Filter::Range|Mask|Predicate, page_validity); decode_masked_required with fast_iter_u56 + trailing_zeros bit loop; required.rs single copy_nonoverlapping for the no-filter no-null case); polars-io/src/parquet/read/read_impl.rs:482 calc_prefilter_cost (prefilter iff num_edges/rg_len <= 0.01, non-nested); polars-stream/src/nodes/io_sources/parquet/row_group_decode.rs:394 row_group_data_to_df_prefiltered (decode predicate columns first in parallel, AND the masks, decode remaining columns with Filter::Mask)

The masked kernels iterate the mask 56 bits at a time (fast_iter_u56), using trailing_zeros to jump to the next selected value, writing straight into the reserved target with raw pointers — selected rows are decoded, skipped rows cost ~1 cycle. The pre/post decision is per row group per column: mask edge density <= 0.01 means clustered selection -> decode-through-mask wins; otherwise decode-all-then-filter. Leading/trailing zero stripping lets kernels degrade to the pure-memcpy path when possible.
findings.maps_to: B1 + B4
findings.our_implementation: arrow-rs 53 won't let us inject a per-value mask into its decoders, but it does accept RowSelection ranges: (1) evaluate predicate columns per row group first (we already do RowFilter, but arrow-rs decodes predicate columns twice — decode them once ourselves, keep them); (2) compute the mask, measure edges/len; if <= ~0.01, convert the mask to a RowSelection and read remaining columns with it; else read all and use one shared filter kernel application. findings.est_payoff: Q06 (122ms, ~1.9% selectivity on date-clustered l_shipdate) and Q19/Q12/Q14 style scans: avoids decoding ~98% of payload column values when selection is clustered by sort order. Realistic 1.3-1.8x on those scans; also removes arrow-rs's double-decode of RowFilter predicate columns everywhere (pure win, ~10-15% of scan time on filtered queries).
findings.effort: Medium (1 week; builds on existing RowFilter/row-group pruning code in src/storage/parquet.rs)

findings.technique: Hot/cold two-tier aggregation: fixed 4096-slot L1-resident table with 2-choice hashing and second-chance eviction in front of partitioned merge
findings.source: .scratch/polars/crates/polars-expr/src/hot_groups/fixed_index_table.rs (2 candidate slots: h1 = hash >> shift, h2 = hash*0xf1357aea2e62a9c5 >> shift; u32 tag per slot; branchless hit check 's1_delta & s2_delta == 0' + select_unpredictable; eviction only if slot's last_access_tag matches, else second chance); .scratch/polars/crates/polars-stream/src/nodes/group_by.rs (DEFAULT_HOT_TABLE_SIZE = 4096; flush_evictions when num_evictions >= ideal morsel size 100_000; evicted keys+partial aggregates hash-partitioned; combine_locals runs one parallel task per partition, pre-sized by CardinalitySketch)
findings.mechanism: Per-thread aggregation runs against a fixed-size table that never grows: hits stay in L1/L2 with flat accumulators; misses evict a slot only on its second consecutive access attempt (last_access_tag), streaming evicted (key, partial-aggregate) pairs into per-partition buffers. Finalize merges each hash partition independently in parallel. High-frequency (skewed) keys stay hot forever; rare keys pass through as pre-aggregated records. Cardinality sketches size the final tables to avoid rehashing.
findings.maps_to: B3 (hash-probe latency floor noted in our gaps; also memory-safety friendly since hot table is fixed size)
findings.our_implementation: In morsel_agg.rs, in front of the thread-local HashMap path: a 4096-entry FixedIndexTable keyed by the raw u64 key/hash with inline flat accumulators; on eviction append (key, partial state) to one of N=num_threads partition vecs; merge partitions in parallel at finalize (we already have range-partitioned merge — this makes its input pre-aggregated). Also adopt a CardinalitySketch (HLL exists via approx_distinct) to pre-size merge maps.
findings.est_payoff: Moderate: biggest effect on skewed/medium-cardinality keys where the main map's random probes dominate (part of our 'radix-partitioned aggregation' roadmap item). Q13/Q16-class queries, and it caps thread-local memory (helps the 64GB-cap rule). Est 10-25% on hashed-agg queries; not a Q18-class win (dense path already near floor at 187ms).
findings.effort: Medium (~1 week, self-contained data structure + merge plumbing)

findings.technique: Join probe output via incremental column builders with bounded output morsels and selectivity-estimated reserves (replace per-batch take+concat)
findings.source: .scratch/polars/crates/polars-stream/src/nodes/joins/equi_join.rs:781 partition_and_probe (probe_limit = get_ideal_morsel_size() = 100_000 rows; probe_subset returns keys_processed so a morsel can be flushed mid-partition via matches_before_limit; build_out/probe_out DataFrameBuilders freeze_reset() per output morsel; 'selectivity_estimate * 1.2 * df_height + 16' reserve; payload rechunked lazily only when there are matches); finalize gathers build payload per hash-partition once (p_payload.gather_extend at :596) so probe-time gathers are partition-local
findings.mechanism: Instead of arrow take per probe batch producing many small arrays later concatenated, matches append into growing typed builders (primitive: unchecked indexed copy; strings: view copy per finding 3). Output morsel size is capped so downstream stays cache-sized regardless of join fanout, and reserve sizes come from a running selectivity estimate so builders rarely reallocate. Build payload is pre-partitioned so probe gathers have partition-locality.
findings.maps_to: B2
findings.our_implementation: In HashJoinExec probe: replace compute::take-per-column-per-batch (hash_join.rs:1074/1700/1708) with per-column builder appends from (build_row, probe_row) match vectors, flushing an 8K-row RecordBatch when full. Keep our concat-once build side. Add running selectivity estimate for reserves. Primitive columns become memcpy-of-values loops; combined with view strings this eliminates the take+concat double materialization.
findings.est_payoff: Attacks the stated B2 bottleneck mechanics directly: fewer allocations (one builder set vs per-batch arrays), no concat pass, no take-index array construction per column. On Q09/Q21/Q20 (1.5s/0.83s/0.94s) where gather dominates, expect 15-30% beyond the view-string win.
findings.effort: Medium (~1 week in hash_join.rs, mechanical but touches all join types)

findings.technique: Whole-column-chunk decode into one target vector; morselize by zero-copy slicing afterwards
findings.source: .scratch/polars/crates/polars-parquet/src/arrow/read/deserialize/utils/mod.rs:461 PageDecoder::collect (single DecodedState spans all pages of the column chunk; kernels append via raw pointers; freeze once); deserialize/README.md (chunk FIFO design); also parquet/handwritten_thrift/ (they hand-rolled the footer thrift parser to cut metadata parse cost)
findings.mechanism: Decode target is allocated once at row-group-column granularity; page kernels write into it with raw pointer appends (no per-page or per-batch array allocation, no builder re-validation). Consumers get morsels by slicing the frozen array — Arrow slices are zero-copy. Metadata parsing avoids generated thrift code overhead.
findings.maps_to: B1
findings.our_implementation: We currently force with_batch_size(8_192) at scan (src/storage/parquet.rs:228,265,308) which makes arrow-rs finalize ~7300 batches/column for 60M rows. Instead: decode with batch_size = row-group size (or 1M), then slice into 8K morsels for compute (keeps the L2-locality win we measured when we went 1M->8K for OPERATORS, while removing per-batch decode finalization). Slicing RecordBatches is zero-copy in arrow-rs.
findings.est_payoff: Modest but broad: saves per-batch allocation/finalization overhead across every scan (~5-10% of decode); on Q01's 250ms decode maybe 15-25ms. Free to try — it's a constant change plus a slicing wrapper. Handwritten thrift is NOT worth it for 8 local files.
findings.effort: Low (1-2 days)

findings.technique: Gandiva-style validity/value decomposition + selection-vector filter->project linkage (skeptical extraction)
findings.source: https://www.dremio.com/blog/announcing-gandiva-initiative-for-apache-arrow/ (validity computed by bitmap intersection, values computed branchlessly for all rows; CASE-100: Java JIT 1361s vs LLVM 15.2s = 89.6x, sum 6.8x — baseline was Java bytecode, NOT a native engine); https://www.dremio.com/blog/gandiva-performance-improvements-production-query/ (81.8x on 15-case nested CASE project stage; planned 'fast code paths for batches which have no nulls'); https://arrow.apache.org/docs/cpp/gandiva/expr_projector_filter.html (Filter emits SelectionVector u16/u32; Projector compiled in selection-vector mode consumes it, avoiding intermediate compaction)
findings.mechanism: Two transferable mechanics, discounting the Java-baseline hype: (1) decompose every expression into unconditional value computation over all rows plus separate validity = AND of input validity bitmaps (null-intolerant ops), eliminating per-row null branches and enabling autovectorization; add no-null fast paths that skip validity work entirely. (2) Filters emit a selection vector consumed directly by downstream projection rather than compacting arrays between operators.
findings.maps_to: B4 (and expression evaluation inside filter.rs)
findings.our_implementation: (1) In filter.rs evaluate_expr: audit scalar/CASE paths that branch on null per row; compute values unconditionally on the values buffer and AND validity bitmaps; add arr.null_count()==0 fast paths. (2) Targeted lazy-compaction: when a filter keeps >~50% of rows (Q01 keeps ~98%), pass the boolean mask to the aggregate consumer (MorselAggregateExec already iterates rows — have accumulator loops apply the mask bit) instead of running the filter kernel over 7 columns x 60M rows. Full JIT (cranelift/LLVM) is NOT justified: we're already native and expressions are not our bottleneck.
findings.est_payoff: Honest estimate: small-moderate overall, but the Q01-shaped case is real — compacting 98%-selective masks copies ~420M values for nothing; mask-aware aggregation saves that full materialization (~30-60ms on Q01, similar on Q12). CASE-heavy speedups won't reproduce because our baseline is already compiled vectorized code, not Java.
findings.effort: Low for no-null fast paths and mask-aware agg (3-5 days); skip JIT entirely

findings.technique: Polars streaming-engine morsel discipline: sequence tokens, source stop tokens, consume-token backpressure, 100k-row morsels, per-pipeline parallel ports
findings.source: .scratch/polars/crates/polars-stream/src/morsel.rs (MorselSeq monotone tokens with reserved LSB; SourceToken::stop for source cutoff e.g. under LIMIT; consume_token WaitToken backpressure; MorselLinearizer = k-way priority merge restoring seq order); polars-config/src/lib.rs:36 DEFAULT_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE = 100_000 rows; nodes/filter.rs (parallelism from per-pipeline ports — inside a pipeline the SEQUENTIAL filter kernel is used, no nested rayon)
findings.mechanism: Each operator spawns one task per pipeline; morsels carry (a) a sequence number so order-sensitive sinks re-linearize with a k-way merge instead of global sorts, (b) a stop token so LIMIT/TopK can halt sources promptly, (c) a consume token so fast producers block instead of queueing unbounded memory. Morsel size is row-count-based (100k), and intra-operator code stays single-threaded — no nested parallelism fighting the scheduler.
findings.maps_to: B2/B3 pipeline plumbing; memory-safety rule (bounded in-flight data)
findings.our_implementation: Adopt: (1) bounded channel depth between morsel stages (we currently collect partitions in several operators — sort.rs/hash_agg.rs collect ALL input first); (2) a stop token checked in ParallelParquetSource so Top-K (Q02/Q03/Q10) stops decoding once the limit heuristic saturates; (3) avoid nested rayon inside per-morsel work where morsel-level parallelism already saturates cores (we've hit this: prescan rayon + operator rayon oversubscription).
findings.est_payoff: Mostly architectural hygiene; concrete wins on early-termination queries (Q02 122ms, Q03 492ms with LIMIT 10-20: stopping scans early can cut their tails) and bounded memory under the 64GB cap. Est 5-15% on limit-bearing queries.
findings.effort: Low-Medium (tokens are simple structs; wiring through operators is incremental)

findings.technique: Dremio C3: NVMe-resident cache of parquet microblocks (sub-row-group, per-column chunks) with RocksDB index — endorses our decoded-sidecar plan rather than replacing it
findings.source: https://www.dremio.com/blog/how-dremio-delivers-fast-queries-on-object-storage-apache-arrow-reflections-and-the-columnar-cloud-cache/ ; https://docs.dremio.com/software/deployment/cloud-cache-config/ (chunks of parquet cached on executor-local NVMe volume, managed by local RocksDB; caches only columns/chunks actually read; claims ~90% object-store I/O reduction, sub-ms local reads)
findings.mechanism: C3 caches raw parquet byte ranges (column-chunk 'microblocks') keyed per file/offset on local NVMe, indexed by RocksDB, populated as a side effect of query reads, evicted LRU-ish. Crucially it caches COMPRESSED parquet bytes — decode still happens per query; the win is purely network I/O, which we don't pay (data already on local NVMe).
findings.maps_to: B5
findings.our_implementation: Skeptical mapping: C3 itself buys us nothing (no network hop to hide). The correct analog for B5 is caching the DECODE, not the bytes: proceed with the Arrow IPC mmap sidecar as the owned format — write each table's columns as uncompressed (or lz4-frame) Arrow IPC with 64-byte-aligned buffers on first read, mmap thereafter; scan becomes pointer casts + our existing zero-copy slicing. Optionally an in-process LRU of decoded ArrayRefs keyed (file, rg, col) for hot columns as an interim step.
findings.est_payoff: Eliminates B1 wholesale on warm data: DuckDB-native vs DuckDB-on-parquet on this machine is 2.94s vs 4.1s (~28% of total), and our decode share is larger (Q01: 250ms of 427ms). Sidecar puts us on the 'native format' side of that gap; plausibly 25-35% off total suite time. This is the single largest B5 lever and Dremio's architecture confirms the read-path-cache framing.
findings.effort: High (owned format + invalidation + memory-safety for mmap under the 64GB cgroup), but already planned

findings.technique: Dremio Reflections: materialized aggregate/sort views as Iceberg tables with automatic planner substitution — note, not a fair-benchmark lever
findings.source: https://www.dremio.com/blog/how-dremio-delivers-fast-queries-on-object-storage-apache-arrow-reflections-and-the-columnar-cloud-cache/ (reflections materialized as Iceberg tables; user picks partition/sort/measures; optimizer substitutes matching reflections transparently; incremental refresh)
findings.mechanism: Precomputed sorted/partitioned/pre-aggregated copies of datasets stored in the lake format; the planner does view-matching to rewrite queries against them. It is materialized-view substitution, not an execution technique.
findings.maps_to: B5 (storage strategy), tangentially B3
findings.our_implementation: Do NOT use for TPC-H numbers (it precomputes the answer — invalidates like-for-like comparison with DuckDB reading raw parquet). Legitimate borrowings: (a) when writing the IPC sidecar, store per-column-chunk zone maps and optionally sort lineitem by l_shipdate (DuckDB benefits from natural clustering the same way — still fair since it's the same data); (b) longer-term, a small view-matching pass over our LogicalPlan for user-defined materializations in the Iceberg integration.
findings.est_payoff: Zero for the benchmark (excluded for fairness). Sorted sidecar + zone maps: improves clustering-dependent pruning (Q06-class range filters) legitimately since we'd sort at ingest like any engine may; small but real.
findings.effort: Low for zone maps in the sidecar; High for general view matching (defer)
